messages:
oliver (customer): Hey team — large customer hitting intermittent streaming cuts. They get the final partial chunk, client reconnects and sometimes sees duplicate tokens/billing hits. Happens only when routed through our ALB -> Cloudflare stack, not when we route direct to origin.

sabrina (support): Thanks, Oliver. Can you paste the minimal repro + headers you used? Which SDK/client?

oliver (customer): Repro: curl from mac -> via cloudflare (prod). Example: curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.customer.example.com/v1/stream
Server sends SSE framed chunks with trailing newline. After ~2m idle (no new tokens for a while) connection drops. Last chunk partial (no newline). Client reconnects and resumes with new token; customer sees 2 requests charged.

matt (sre): Do you have any edge logs or ALB logs around the disconnect? Specifically: ALB target_response_time, elb_status_code, and TCP half-close events.

oliver (customer): Attached (paste): 
```
ALB: request_id=abc123 elb_status=200 target_status=200 target_response_time=120.345
Cloudflare: 522/timeout? we see a gated timeout then origin reconnect
Client: receives last chunk: "data: ...partial" then connection close
```

sabrina (support): Hmm. Two common packing causes: buffering at Cloudflare/nginx (accidental aggregation) and ALB idle timeout/half-close. Do you set any server-side keepalive/heartbeat?

oliver (customer): No explicit heartbeat, we only push tokens when user types.

jamie (eng-infra): Quick checklist: 1) confirm response has `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream` 2) ensure `Connection: keep-alive` preserved across proxies 3) disable gzip on streaming route 4) set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` if behind nginx 5) bump ALB idle timeout > expected quiet windows (default 60s).

matt (sre): Also check ALB `deregistration_delay` and target group `slow_start`. ALB can half-close sockets (FIN) and keep client unaware leading to truncated last bytes. Cloudflare may then try to re-issue and client reconnect logic causes double-charge.

oliver (customer): Ok trying: add 15s heartbeat ping `: ping\n\n` between events and disable gzip. Any way to reproduce quickly inside our infra?

sabrina (support): Yes — quick repro curl that forces no-buffering: `curl -v --no-buffer https://.../stream` and on server `printf "data: first\n\n"; sleep 90; printf "data: second\n\n"` — if you see first but not second when proxied, proxy is buffering or timing out.

jamie (eng-infra): Also run `ncat -l 8080 --keep-open` and `curl --raw` to emulate raw TCP to see where the FIN originates. If ALB closes the backend then you'll see a FIN from elb.

matt (sre): From logs: ALB target_response_time=120s in snippet — that suggests connection sat idle ~2m. Default ALB idle timeout = 60s, but Cloudflare adds its own. If the client->cloudflare idle > CF limit it will reset. Looks like a mismatch chain: CF idle ~100s, ALB 60s, app sends nothing until later => ALB closes to origin, CF holds and then tries to reconnect -> partial chunk.

sabrina (support): Short-term mitigation: 1) add app-side heartbeat at <=30s 2) set ALB idle timeout to 300s for this target group (if you can) 3) set `Connection: keep-alive` and disable buffering (nginx/Envoy flags) 4) set `Cache-Control: no-transform` 5) ensure no intermediate proxy gzips or rewrites chunk boundaries.

oliver (customer): We changed ALB timeout to 300s and pushed a heartbeat every 20s. After a few hours, looks stable. Client sees single charge.

jamie (eng-infra): Recommended infra follow-up: add an automated e2e test that runs a streaming call through ALB+Cloudflare every night and asserts no mid-stream disconnects for 5 minutes. We'll open a ticket.

matt (sre): Opening infra ticket: TG-1123 to tighten observability: instrument TCP FIN/RESET counts per target and surface in Console.

sabrina (support): Great. Oliver, will you keep us posted? If this recurs we'll need packet-level traces and `strace` on the service process to capture the exact write/close ordering.

oliver (customer): Will do. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
